text: Migrated kernel, core, protocol and all seven interpreter modules to ByteVector across four commits. No source outside two documented places still names Vector[Byte]: the benchmark that compares representations, and the circe bridge in AgentDomainJson that deliberately preserves the derived codecs' numeric wire array. 431 tests pass across 13 modules with every committed golden literal untouched, and scalafmtCheckAll is clean. The measured result is in the AFTER note: retained footprint drops from 2.4x the backing array to 1.0x, and the array-conversion boundary goes from 6.8x slower than Array.clone to parity. FrameDecoder.feed was flat before and stays flat; the quadratic premise in this description was refuted by measurement rather than fixed. This unblocks P6f.12, which was the primary reason to sequence it first: the codec laws can now be written once against one byte representation.
